test_title: PYST 10: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A train runs at a speed of 60 km/h. How much time will it take to cover a distance of 180 km?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Time = 180 ÷ 60

Time = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the train = 60 km/h

Distance to be covered = 180 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c70bb44f48ea97553332b1552da160ec65178bb8e6893de7b6f2ad013105c4f8.png] 

⇒ Distance = 180 km

⇒ Speed = 60 km/h

⇒ Time = 180 ÷ 60

⇒ Time = 3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distance Formula

Distance is the product of speed and time: Distance = Speed × Time.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).
